titles.617: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — Israel's idolatry called Jeroboam's sin as first author (parallel to Adam)
titles.618: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — Rom 5: death passed to all because all sinned; omnes same men same way
titles.619: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — otherwise four-term syllogism; conclusion omnes = persons distinct from Adam
titles.620: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — distinct persons did not commit Adam's one numerical actual sin (nor one numerical death)
titles.621: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR Resp — hard to see how that proves Adam's-sin imputation; no confused hypostasis
titles.622: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC tip — will explain; does not impugn mediate/consequent imputation after corruption

latin.617: Sic, communis omnium peccatum Ieroboami vocatur, non autem Iudaeorum Israelis idolatria tam alicuius alterius regis, propterea quod primus illius autor Ieroboamus fuerat.
latin.618: Interim nonne vides omnes homines eodem modo accipi ab Apostolo, cum in eos mortem transire, & cum eos peccasse dicit? Mors, inquit, in omnes transiit, quoniam omnes peccaverunt. Utrobique vox omnes eosdem homines, eodem modo, significat.
latin.619: Alioqui vitiosus esset Apostoli syllogismus, & ex quatuor terminis componeretur, quem sic forms: Quicumque peccaverunt, in eos mors transiit; Omnes peccaverunt; Igitur in omnes mors transiit. Nam in conclusione vox omnes notat personas omnium hominum inter se & a persona Adami distinctas & separatas. Ergo necesse est ut in minore eadem vox omnium itidem hominum personas distinctas & separatas cum inter se tum ab Adamo significet.
latin.620: Iam autem manifestum est, omnium hominum personas distinctas & separatas a persona Adami non commisisse peccatum illud actuale unum idemque numero quod Adamus commisit, & tam impossibile esse ut omnium personarum generis humani sit unicum numero peccatum actuale, quam ut sit unica numero mors omnium.
latin.621: GAR. Resp. Huius rationis vim satis ad assignandam peccati Adami imputationem videre difficile est & dicere. Nam aut longe fallor, aut nemo eorum qui pro hac imputatione pugnant, unquam somniavit personam suam, vel alterius cuiuscumque hominis, esse confusam cum persona Adami, aut ita indistinctam, ut in unum ὑπόστασιν cum ea coaluerit. Hoc ne quidem animo concipi potest. &c.
latin.622: PLAC. Quandoquidem videre huius rationis vim Vir doctus non potuit, eam explicabo. Meminerit igitur, Lector, si placet, me non impugnare imputationem mediatam seu consequentem, quae cuiusque existentia & corruptione posterior est.

pass_a.617: Placeus's Jeroboam parallel: Israel's idolatry is named Jeroboam's sin because he was first author—not some later king's—setting up how a first source can name a common sin.
pass_a.618: He turns to Rom 5: the Apostle takes the same 'all' the same way for death's transit and for 'they sinned.' 'Death passed to all because all sinned' keeps one set of persons in view.
pass_a.619: Else Paul's argument is a four-term fallacy. Schematized: whoever sinned, death entered them; all sinned; so death entered all. The conclusion's 'all' means persons distinct from Adam—so the minor's 'all' must mean those same distinct persons.
pass_a.620: But those distinct persons did not commit Adam's one numerical actual sin. One numerical actual sin of every human person is as impossible as one numerical death of everyone. Tip of the syllogism press.
pass_a.621: Garrigues answers that Placeus's reason hardly assigns Adam's-sin imputation. No champion of that view, he says, ever dreamed his person (or anyone's) fused with Adam into one hypostasis—such confusion is not even thinkable.
pass_a.622: Tip: Placeus will unpack the argument's force. He marks what he is not attacking—mediate/consequent imputation after each one's existence and corruption—before the immediate/antecedent target. Tip before that explanation.

617: So the common sin of all is called Jeroboam's sin—not Israel's idolatry as of some other king—because Jeroboam had been its first author.
618: Meanwhile, do you not see that all men are taken in the same way by the Apostle, both when death passes into them and when he says they sinned? Death, he says, passed into all, because all sinned. In both places the word "all" signifies the same men, in the same way.
619: Otherwise the Apostle's syllogism would be faulty and composed of four terms, which you may form thus: Whoever sinned, into them death passed; all sinned; therefore into all death passed. For in the conclusion the word "all" marks the persons of all men, distinct among themselves and from Adam's person. So in the minor the same word must likewise signify the distinct and separate persons of all men, both among themselves and from Adam.
620: But it is already plain that the distinct and separate persons of all men, apart from Adam's person, did not commit that one actual sin, one and the same in number, which Adam committed. And it is as impossible that there should be one numerical actual sin of all the persons of the human race as that there should be one numerical death of all.
621: GAR. Resp. It is hard enough to see and say how the force of this reason assigns the imputation of Adam's sin. For either I am far wrong, or none of those who fight for this imputation ever dreamed that his own person, or any other man's, is confused with Adam's person, or so indistinct as to have coalesced into one hypostasis with him. That cannot even be conceived in the mind. Etc.
622: PLAC. Since the learned man could not see the force of this reason, I will explain it. Let the reader remember, if he will, that I am not attacking mediate or consequent imputation, which is later than each one's existence and corruption.

617.choice: First author names the common sin

618.choice: Same all for death-transit and peccaverunt

619.choice: Four-term risk; conclusion all = distinct persons

620.choice: Distinct persons ≠ Adam's one numerical act

621.choice: Doesn't prove imputation; no hypostatic fusion
